section: 8 size effects, calibration against the lattice
finding: Eringen's 0.39 is exactly where the manuscript says: the Born-Karman zone-boundary match, and the value is 0.39
evidence: Eringen (1983) p. 4705: 'By matching a = (1 + e0^2 a^2 k^2)^-1 obtained this way with Eq. (3.20) at the end of the Brillouin zone, we obtain a curve which approximates the atomic dispersion curve quite well ... wa/co = ka(1 + e0^2 k^2 a^2)^-1/2 (Nonlocal), wa/co = 2 sin(ka/2) (Lattice Dynamics) (3.22). The matching is perfect at ka = pi, which leads to e0 ~ 0.39. (3.23) The maximum error is of the order of 6% in |ka| < pi.' Eq. (3.20) is the Born-Karman a(k) = (2/k^2a^2)(1 - cos ka)

finding: The second calibration in the same paragraph, xi^2 = a^2/12 (xi = 0.289a), is also Eringen's own expansion, so the zone-boundary vs long-wavelength contrast is sourced, not reconstructed

The paragraph presents 0.39 as the Eringen value for the whole paper, but in the same paper Eringen calibrates his SURFACE-wave (Rayleigh) results against Wallis-Gazis KCl with e0 = 0.31, not 0.39; since this review applies the length to Rayleigh waves, a reader may take 0.39 as the surface-wave value
should_be: add a clause: 0.39 is the bulk/zone-boundary match, whereas Eringen's own surface-wave comparison used e0 = 0.31
evidence: Eringen (1983) p. 4709: 'To provide a comparison of these results with the lattice dynamic calculations, we divide the abscissa and ordinate of Fig. 4 by e0 = 0.31. ... Comparison with atomic lattice dynamic calculations carried out by Wallis and Gazis for KCl is excellent.' Also p. 4707: 'the match of the dispersion curves were provided for the value of e0 = 0.39 with an error less than 6%'
